questions.question: Which landmark case was Justice A N Grover a part of, as highlighted during the book launch of The Unyielding Judge: The Life and Legacy of Justice A N Grover?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kesavananda Bharti case.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Attorney General R Venkataramani spoke at the book launch of *The Unyielding Judge: The Life and Legacy of Justice A N Grover* by Gauri Grover, emphasizing a judge's role in upholding human values.**
 
• **Justice A N Grover was part of the 13-judge constitutional bench in the 1973 Kesavananda Bharti case.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The Kesavananda Bharti case upheld the basic structure doctrine, ensuring that the Constitution's core principles cannot be amended by Parliament.
 
• Justice A N Grover contributed to India's constitutional history and was recognized for his fearlessness and adherence to values.
 
• The book *The Unyielding Judge* explores Justice Grover's legacy in constitutional law.
 
• Other speakers at the event included Justice (retd) S K Katriar and senior advocate Salman Khurshid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Kesavananda Bharti Case (1973):__

 __
 
• A landmark case in Indian constitutional law where the Supreme Court established the basic structure doctrine.
 
• The doctrine ensures that certain core principles of the Constitution, like democracy, federalism, and secularism, cannot be amended by Parliament.
 
 
 
• Justice A N Grover:__
 
 
• Known for his significant contributions to India's constitutional history.
 
• Part of major constitutional cases that shaped India's judiciary and governance.

questions.question: Who edited the book 'English Poetry from Bihar' launched in New Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prof. Ram Bhagwan Singh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The book features 22 poets from Bihar who wrote or write in English, including both historical and contemporary poets.
 
• Prof. Ram Bhagwan Singh, the editor, is a retired professor of English from Ranchi University and a bilingual writer, translator, and critic.
 
• Prominent contributors include Avadh Bihari Lall, Tabish Khair, Abhay K, Kalpana Singh-Chitnis, and Surabhi Sonam.
 
• The anthology highlights the contribution of Bihari poets to English literature and complements the earlier work, 'The Book of Bihari Literature.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **About Prof. Ram Bhagwan Singh:**__

 __
 
• Born in 1941, he retired as a professor of English from Ranchi University in 2001.
 
• He is known for his bilingual works, translations, and weekly columns in educational journals.
 
 
 
• **Notable Contributors to the Anthology:**__
 __
 
• Avadh Bihari Lall (1866-1921): A historical poet from Bihar.
 
• Abhay K: Contemporary poet, whose nine poems, including 'Nalanda,' feature in the anthology.
 
• Kalpana Singh-Chitnis and Surabhi Sonam: Among the modern poets contributing to English literature from Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Book:**__
 
 
• Documents the contribution of Bihari poets to English literature.
 
• A valuable resource for libraries and literary enthusiasts interested in regional contributions to global literature.

questions.question: What is the key theme of Anand Neelakantan's upcoming book "Many Ramayanas, Many Lessons"?

options.text: A single truth about the Ramayana as presented by Valmiki
An exploration of the Ramayana's plurality and its retellings across cultures and geographies
A detailed analysis of the Bahubali trilogy as inspired by the Ramayana
A modern retelling of the Ramayana focusing on Rama's journey exclusively

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**An exploration of the Ramayana's plurality and its retellings across cultures and geographies**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Anand Neelakantan's book 'Many Ramayanas Many Lessons' to be published.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The book explores how the Ramayana is not just a single story but a symphony of stories spanning centuries, cultures, and languages.
 
• It highlights the plurality of the epic, discussing versions from Southeast Asia, Central Asia, and beyond.
 
• Anand Neelakantan provides fresh perspectives on characters and events, such as Surpanakha being portrayed as a victim and the absence of Lakshmana Rekha in Valmiki's version.
 
• The book emphasizes the enduring wisdom and lessons derived from the Ramayana's many retellings across different traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Anand Neelakantan is a renowned author known for his counter-telling of Indian epics, including works like "Asura" and the Bahubali trilogy.
 
• His book celebrates the diversity and richness of the Ramayana tradition, showcasing variations like Sita being Ravana's daughter in Thai and Tibetan versions.
 
• HarperCollins describes the book as a groundbreaking work that blends meticulous research with storytelling to present the Ramayana in a new light.
 
• The Ramayana's interpretations vary significantly across cultures, offering unique lessons and truths relevant to specific geographies and times.
 
• The book is based on Neelakantan's popular audiobook of the same name and aims to revive interest in the lesser-known versions of the epic.

questions.question: Which book, authored by Rajesh Talwar critiques Mahatma Gandhi's Hind Swaraj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Mahatma’s Manifesto.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Author-playwright Rajesh Talwar has released a book titled "The Mahatma’s Manifesto."**
 
• The book critiques Mahatma Gandhi’s *Hind Swaraj* and highlights contradictions in his views on modernity, industrialization, and Western thought.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• *Hind Swaraj* was written by Mahatma Gandhi in November 1909 during his journey from England to South Africa.
 
• The book was banned by the British in 1910 as it called for India’s independence from imperial rule.
 
• Talwar’s book critically examines Gandhi’s rejection of industrialization and Western thought.
 
• "The Mahatma’s Manifesto" has been published by Om Publications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ***Hind Swaraj***__

 __
 
• One of Mahatma Gandhi’s most significant works, outlining his vision of self-rule.
 
• Argues for Indian self-reliance, non-violence, and rejection of Western civilization.
 
• Banned by the British in 1910 for its anti-imperialist stance.
 
 
 
• **Rajesh Talwar**__
 __
 
• An author and playwright known for works on socio-political themes.
 
• His books often provide critical perspectives on historical and contemporary issues.
 
 
 
• **Om Publications**__
 
 
• A publishing house known for books on history, politics, and social thought.
